gates/ga.json.requirement: No Patch/Skip code, generated artifacts, tests, or engine dependencies in the product; provenance/dependency review passed.
Owned compiler integration, UI engine, bridges, interpreter, updater, and hosted workflow are implemented and supported.
Public support matrix, limitation list, version policy, licensing/notices, and migration contract match actual behavior.
Product naming/trademarks, customer terms, privacy material, and third-party redistribution obligations are reviewed.
A new developer can create and locally run a shared Swift app on physical iOS and Android using public documentation.

FieldLog's required native UI, state, navigation, input, and accessibility matrix passes on both platforms. Reference screens must meet shared-theme design parity per section8.3, reviewed side by side on physical iOS/Android devices.
The published language/runtime/capability profile passes in native and guest modes without silent feature omission.
Compiler, guest, bridge, and native failures map to actionable original-source diagnostics.
All first-party capability families in Section 9 pass their platform-specific behavior/permission tests.
Existing-app migration and native-screen embedding work for an independent Swift project.
Local/exported CI can build and maintain FieldLog independently of hosted service availability.
Meaningful logic and UI updates reach already-installed binaries on both platforms without reinstalling them.
Client and server reject wrong app, environment, runtime, signature, protocol, capability, size, and replayed assignment.
Interruption at every download/activation transition preserves a launchable healthy implementation.
Failed guest startup is quarantined; offline recovery works without an infinite crash loop.
Rollback preserves saved drafts, records, uploads, and compatible schema behavior; external effects are reconciled correctly.
Key rotation/revocation, old offline clients, and root-compromise limitations are exercised and documented.
Staged promotion/halt and dual-platform cohort targeting work across mixed native binary versions.
New native capabilities/permissions/SDKs correctly require a store build.

Elixir/Oban orchestration and isolated macOS/iOS and Android builds produce signed, traceable artifacts with usable logs and debugging symbols; Cloudflare workers or recorded hosting exceptions pass resource/isolation/lifecycle qualification.
Store integrations reach verified ready-for-testing and available states; provider errors are accurately represented.
SolidJS console on Cloudflare and Phoenix API support onboarding, teams, permissions, SSO, audit export, customer keys, and dedicated-runner workflows end to end.
Stripe billing, Neon usage reconciliation, usage caps, credits, cancellation, export/deletion, and support workflows pass realistic account and duplicate/out-of-order webhook cases.

Phoenix API/CLI/SolidJS behavior agrees; domain writes and Oban enqueue are atomic; publishing and chargeable actions remain idempotent under redelivery and worker failures, including migration parity with existing Go contracts.
Independent VM/bridge/update/signing/tenant-isolation review has no unresolved launch-blocking findings.
Applicable standards-profile conformance, differential tests, fuzzing, and resource-limit tests pass.
Performance, memory, patch size, sharing, and real-change OTA coverage meet the approved budgets with published methodology.
Device/OS/accessibility/localization matrix passes, with physical evidence for performance and native capabilities.
Service objectives have sufficient operating/load-test evidence, including Cloudflare container stop/wake with no user traffic and Neon/Oban reconnect behavior; low-volume uncertainty is disclosed.
Neon backup restoration/region-loss, R2/CDN isolation/freshness, separate worker/signer loss, Stripe reconciliation, compromised publisher, and bad-release drills are complete.
Alerting, accountable escalation, status page, incident communication, and security response are configured and rehearsed.
D0–D8 complete; FieldLog is available through real iOS/Android store distribution with transparent update behavior.
FieldLog has repeated real production use, a reviewed 20-change OTA coverage corpus, and verified recovery across the required scenarios.
Two independently authored external apps qualify, including an existing Swift app migration.
Documentation and onboarding have been tested by developers outside the engine team.
Paid-pilot evidence and contribution-margin model support the commercial offering; weak demand is explicitly reviewed.
SDK upgrade, native release, OTA release, rollback, and customer-exit guides are complete and exercised.
Every failed/blocked mandatory item is resolved; release approval references actual evidence rather than planned work.
